content: Efavirenz is metabolized by the hepatic enzyme CYP2B6, and its levels or effects can be reduced by rifampin, which induces metabolism through the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised when these drugs are co-administered. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of elacestrant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin increases the metabolism of elafibranor, reducing its levels or effects. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Elagolix increases rifampin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, while rifampin increases elagolix levels through other mechanisms. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Rifampin also decreases elagolix levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use of elagolix 150 mg daily with rifampin should be limited to six months. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, which can compromise therapeutic efficacy. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of reduced antiviral response. Rifampin decreases eletriptan levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug, with close monitoring. Eliglustat increases rifampin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter, while rifampin reduces eliglustat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Rifampin reduces eltrombopag levels by inducing CYP1A2 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Eltrombopag also increases rifampin levels by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised due to potential interactions involving OATP transporter protein inhibition. Rifampin increases eluxadoline levels by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administered with OATP1B1 inhibitors, reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg twice daily. Rifampin reduces elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, which may lead to loss of therapeutic effect and potential resistance. This combination is contraindicated. Rifampin decreases enalapril levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Enasidenib increases rifampin levels through other mechanisms. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dosage of sensitive OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates to minimize toxicity risks. Rifampin reduces encorafenib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Encorafenib, an OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 inhibitor, may increase the concentration and toxicity of OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 substrates. Rifampin reduces enfortumab vedotin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin decreases entrectinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces enzalutamide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider using an alternative drug with minimal CYP3A4 induction potential. If unavoidable, increase the enzalutamide dose from 160 mg to 240 mg daily. If the CYP3A4 inducer is discontinued, revert to the original enzalutamide dose. Rifampin reduces eplerenone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin decreases erdafitinib levels by altering its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erdafitinib increases rifampin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. If co-administration is unavoidable, separate administration by at least six hours. Rifampin reduces ergotamine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases erlotinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces erythromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases escitalopram levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin reduces esomeprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin decreases estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels of conjugated synthetic estrogens and esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin decreases eszopiclone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended, as rifampin reduces zopiclone AUC by 80%, and a similar effect is expected with eszopiclone. Ethanol reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and is more likely with chronic ethanol use. Rifampin decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use a nonhormonal contraceptive method. Rifampin reduces ethosuximide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Rifampin decreases ethotoin levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin reduces etonogestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases etoposide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin reduces etrasimod levels by inducing CYP3A4, CYP2C8, and CYP2C9 metabolism. Rifampin decreases etravirine levels by inducing CYP3A4, CYP2C19, and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces eucalyptus levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin decreases everolimus levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. This combination is contraindicated. Rifampin reduces exemestane levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. For patients receiving exemestane with a potent CYP3A4 inducer, the recommended dose is 50 mg daily after a meal. Rifampin decreases fedratinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces felbamate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases felodipine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces fenfluramine levels through other mechanisms. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended, as co-administration with serotonin-increasing drugs may increase the risk of serotonin syndrome. Rifampin decreases fentanyl levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to reduced efficacy or withdrawal symptoms in dependent patients. After stopping a CYP3A4 inducer, fentanyl plasma concentrations may increase, prolonging therapeutic and adverse effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Rifampin reduces fesoterodine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin increases fexinidazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases fexofenadine levels by inducing the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin reduces finasteride levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin decreases finerenone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces flibanserin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin decreases fluconazole levels by increasing its metabolism. Fluconazole reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Rifampin reduces fludrocortisone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases flurazepam levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin reduces flurbiprofen levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin increases fluvastatin toxicity through other mechanisms while reducing its levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin decreases fosamprenavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Rifampin reduces fosaprepitant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases fosinopril levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin reduces fosphenytoin levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Fostamatinib increases rifampin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter, while rifampin reduces fostamatinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases fostemsavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated, as it may lead to loss of virologic response and resistance. Rifampin reduces frovatriptan levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin decreases fruquintinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces futibatinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases ganaxolone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces gefitinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Increase gefitinib to 500 mg daily if co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inducer. Resume the standard dose of 250 mg daily seven days after discontinuing the inducer. Rifampin decreases gentamicin levels by inducing the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin reduces gepirone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases gilteritinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces glasdegib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Rifampin reduces glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin decreases guanfacine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Rifampin reduces haloperidol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Rifampin decreases hydrocodone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Rifampin reduces hydrocortisone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces ibrutinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases ibuprofen levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin reduces idelalisib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin increases ifosfamide toxicity by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised.
